irreducible_def integral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → G) : G :=
  if _ : CompleteSpace G then
    if hf : Integrable f μ then L1.integral (hf.toL1 f) else 0
  else 0

instance [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] :
    HMul (Matrix l m α) (Matrix m n α) (Matrix l n α) where
  hMul M N := fun i k => (fun j => M i j) ⬝ᵥ fun j => N j k

theorem mul_apply [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] {M : Matrix l m α} {N : Matrix m n α}
    {i k} : (M * N) i k = ∑ j, M i j * N j k :=
  rfl

instance [Fintype n] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] : Mul (Matrix n n α) where
  mul M N := M * N

meaning: E is real Euclidean space with q+1 coordinates, its Euclidean norm and Borel sigma-algebra. WithLp.ofLp exposes coordinates.
The actual law is stdGaussian E, defined as the orthonormal-basis pushforward of independent gaussianReal 0 1 coordinates. Gaussian moment and symmetry certificates are not premises.

Matrix indices are finite. vecMulVec v v has entries v_i v_j. The identity is the real diagonal identity. Kronecker indices place Gaussian coordinates first and deterministic feature coordinates second.

The declared matrix norm is the canonical Euclidean L2 operator norm, with its finite-dimensional topology. Integrable is a.e. strong measurability plus finite norm integral. Both matrix integrabilities are conclusions. The Bochner nonintegrable default is zero.
Ordinary matrix multiplication is the finite sum of products. squared x is Y x multiplied by itself, without entrywise squaring.
PosSemidef M asserts Hermitian symmetry and nonnegative quadratic forms for every finitely supported vector. On the finite real paired index set this is the Loewner upper-minus-lower conclusion.

The feature length is explicitly the sum of squared real coordinates, avoiding any function-space norm convention. The cutoff uses the closed event R≤L. No retained-probability normalization is introduced.
The midpoint grid uses source row i_src=i.val+1 and frequencies k=0,...,q. The constant coordinate is one and the higher coordinates are sqrt(2) cos(k theta_i). q=0 gives one coordinate.
